result.rationale: In deleteEvent the diff changes the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find compares against undefined and always yields undefined, making calendarId undefined where it previously resolved to the destination calendar's externalId. Same pattern in updateEvent. This drops the destination-calendar fallback for legacy references, plausibly deleting/updating against the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `deleteEvent` computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (e.g., legacy references without it), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains the correct calendar. The code then falls back to the default ("primary"), so deletions target the wrong calendar and can leave the real event orphaned. (The same pattern appears in `updateEvent` too.)
